title: Ring regions: split the surface into the regions rings enclose and select them topologically (between rings, distal of a ring)
description:
User request 2026-10-03, follow-on to the ring tool (CRAW-28, CRAW-30). A set of closed rings divides a surface into regions: on the crawfish, rings 1 to 4 around a leg cut it into the thigh, the shin and so on. Make those regions first-class: compute them, and let the user select them topologically.

Region computation. Given the surface and a set of ring mark loops (spline_ring, loop_through_points, ring_candidates output), split the faces into connected components with the ring edges as walls (flood fill across faces whose shared edge is not a ring edge; PATCH-81 did the same for LyonLayoutDecomposer). Each region records which rings bound it and on which side, so 'the region between ring 2 and ring 3' and 'everything distal of ring 4' are queries rather than picks. A ring that does not close, or two rings that cross, should be reported rather than producing leaks: report the region count and the bounding rings per region.

Selection. A DSL node (for example ring_regions, producing a per-face region label the way tag_geometry and the CRAW-6 label nodes do), plus an interactive pick: click a region to select it, Shift+click to add more, and a 'between rings' pick that selects every region bounded by the chosen rings. Decide whether this lives in the ring tool or in a separate decomposition tool that takes the rings as input (the user leans towards a decomposition tool). The selection should feed the existing selection and labelling nodes so that downstream steps (part labels in CRAW-24, per-region quad layout in the companion ticket) consume it.

Related: CRAW-24 already flood-fills regions between rings to transfer part labels across a collection; share the region computation with it rather than writing two.

Rework 2026-10-03 (user review before landing):
1. No permanent on-screen text. Remove the top-left block ("N regions, M selected / select=..."). Where status text should go in general is VIEW-13; until then log to the terminal.
2. Ring numbers behave exactly like the ring tool's. They jump around while orbiting in the region scene; draw them with the ring tool's own label code (shared, not copied), so placement, depth handling and the N show/hide toggle (hidden by default, CRAW-36) are the same.
3. One editing scene with switchable tools instead of a separate ring-regions scene. The ring tool and the region-select tool are tools in one mesh editing scene (today's ring-tool scene, renamed if that reads better), with a key and a control hint to switch the active tool, and room for more tools later. Each tool owns its own mouse and key bindings while it is active; switching keeps the rings and the region selection. Remove the separate ring-regions scene and its launch entry.
4. Remove saving the selection (Ctrl+S writing select= into the .dsl). Regions are recomputed from the rings on every load, so a saved selection adds nothing the user wants; Ctrl+S in the editing scene saves rings only.
5. Remove the between-rings mode (B key and the 'between' select term). Research on the build transcript: plain click and Shift+click hit first time on every try, while between-rings needed two redefinitions on fertility (no ring separates the surface; it has four handles) and once selected all 20 regions; with its fallback it reduces to "the regions both rings bound", which one click selects directly. Keep the ring_regions node and its region / point select terms for DSL and agent use (the extraction follow-up names a region that way).
6. The model list: VIEW-12 makes the list and the [ / ] keys work in every mesh-node scene; sync onto it when it lands rather than fixing it here.

Round 3, 2026-10-03 (user review):
7. Rings show through the model (fertility rings 12 and 9 in the region tool, and loops such as 6 and 10 in the ring tool: the far half of the loop is visible through the body). The ring lines go through MeshOverlayRuntime.setLineGroups -> SurfaceFaceLocator.appendSegments, which looks up the nearest face to each segment's midpoint within onSurfaceDistance; a miss leaves zero normals, which mesh_line.fs never drops. Mesh edges and embedded arcs carry exact face normals from topology instead. First confirm the cause (count zero-normal or wrong-face segments per ring on fertility), then fix at the root: carry the faces the tracer already knows (SurfaceSplineTracer.tracedRing() TracedSurfacePath vertex/edge crossings) on SurfaceSpline and build each ring segment's LineSet normals from them, the way LineSet.edge/vertexStep do. No depth bias. Keeping the crossings on SurfaceSpline is also the first step CRAW-37 needs.
8. An Orbit tool: a third tool in the editing scene that only orbits, pans and zooms the camera and changes no state (no clicks, drags or keys that edit rings, anchors or the selection). The scene opens with the Orbit tool active; Tab cycles Orbit -> Ring -> Regions.

9. The editing scene still inherits the mesh viewer's patch and collection controls: P patch overlay, Shift+P shader mode, D patch decomposer, K keep/reject collection member (MeshNodeViewerScene.setControls, MeshViewerKeyGuy). Remove them from the editing scene, keys and hints, with no patch decomposition run or drawn there; keep [ / ] model list, Z wireframe and camera. The plain mesh viewer keeps them.

10. Camera not framed on open (user, 2026-10-03): the editing scene (ring-tool) opens with the orbit at the default distance (3.5) against fertility's radius of about 107, so the screen is filled by a close-up of the surface; every other mesh-node scene frames the whole model. Agents have been working around it with ixdar-cli frame. Find the cause (candidates: MeshNodeViewerScene's graph load calls frameMesh, which returns early while orbitMouse is null, and initInput later sets CAMERA_DISTANCE_DEFAULT; or uploadGraphOutput's path calls frameCamera without frameMesh; or a tool's activate touching the orbit) and fix it so the scene frames the model on open and on every model switch, like the plain mesh viewer.

Round 4, 2026-10-03 (user review):
11. Replace Tab cycling with one direct key per tool: Ctrl+R ring tool, Ctrl+T segmentation (region select) tool. Esc in any tool returns to the Orbit tool (switching keeps the tool's state, so an open ring draft stays open until the user discards it in the ring tool); Esc in the Orbit tool does nothing. Remove Tab.
12. The menu moves off Esc to Ctrl+I in the editing scene, always available whatever the active tool, and no tool may bind Ctrl+I. Check every binding in the scene (viewer, tools, terminal ~) for conflicts with Ctrl+R, Ctrl+T and Ctrl+I and list them in the report.
Per-tool control sections in the menu are a separate ticket; menu text wrapping is fixed in VIEW-12.
definition-of-done:
1. A ring_regions node labels every face of fertility with the user's saved rings by region and reports the region count and each region's bounding rings. 2. An open or crossing ring is reported by name, not leaked through. 3. Clicking a region selects it, Shift+click adds more, and 'between rings' selects the regions those rings bound; a launch entry and screenshots in tmp/ show each. 4. CRAW-24's flood fill uses the same region computation.

5. RingRegions.regionCount (the public field the report and the ui/mesh/regions route read) is the acceptance number for item 1 and stays.

Rework (2026-10-03): R1. No permanent text on screen in the editing scene. R2. Ring numbers in the region tool come from the ring tool's label code and do not jump while orbiting (screenshots at two orbit angles). R3. One editing scene: a key switches between the ring tool and the region tool, listed in the control hints; the separate ring-regions scene is gone. R4. No selection save and no between-rings mode remain. R5. Build checkstyle-green; tests pass.

R6. On fertility at several orbit angles, no ring segment on the far side of the body is visible (screenshots in both tools, including rings 6, 9, 10 and 12); report the zero-normal segment count before and after. R7. The scene opens in the Orbit tool; clicking and dragging there only moves the camera, and the ring and region state is unchanged (ui-state before and after).

R8. The editing scene's control hints list none of P, Shift+P, D or K, those keys do nothing there, and no patch decomposition runs (log); the mesh viewer still has them.

R9. Launching the user's 'Ring Tool' entry and the CRAW-32 entry shows the whole model framed with no frame command; switching models with [ / ] frames each one; orbit state logged on open matches the plain mesh viewer's for the same .dsl.

R10. Ctrl+R and Ctrl+T switch straight to their tool from any tool, Esc returns to Orbit from either, Tab does nothing; Ctrl+I opens and closes the menu from every tool; no key conflicts (listed); hints updated; screenshots and ui-state per switch.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test: a cylinder with three rings gives four regions with the right bounding rings. 2. Unit test: an open ring is reported and makes no extra region. 3. F5 on fertility: select the region between two leg rings and screenshot it.
changes-made:
2026-10-03 CRAW-32 implemented in worktree craw-32 (uncommitted). Shared engine RingRegions (geometry/mesh/data): floods faces with every closed ring's edges as walls, records each region's bounding rings and, per separating ring, its distal (smaller-area) or proximal side; reports open rings (loose ends, left out of the walls), rings that mark no edge, self-meeting rings, crossing rings, non-separating rings (loops around a handle) and rings that touch or cross at shared vertices. DSL node ring_regions(geometry, labels="", select="", tag="") -> geometry (+_ring_regions slot, +tag), region (per-face INT), selection (per-face BOOLEAN for separate_geometry/delete_geometry FACE), region_count, report. select terms: "region N", "point x,y,z", "between ring_a ring_b" (smallest piece the chosen rings cut off that borders all of them; falls back to the regions every chosen ring bounds when they cut nothing off, as on fertility's handles). Interactive tool: new scene ring-regions (scenes/regions/RingRegionScene + RingRegionTool), not in RingTool: click selects a region, Shift+click adds/drops, B = between mode (clicks pick the nearest bounding ring), C clears, Ctrl+S writes/updates `regions = ring_regions(..., select="...")` in the working .dsl, which reloads with the selection. Route GET /mesh/regions (ixdar-cli regions).
Verification: unit RingRegionsTest 4/4 (capped cylinder with 3 rings -> 4 regions with the right bounding rings and sides; open ring reported and no extra region; node outputs + tag; torus handle with 2 non-separating rings -> between selects the stretch). Full unit suite 344/0 failures; mvn -q compile clean. Fertility (fertility_rings.dsl, 18 rings, tested on a tmp copy): 20 regions, all 18 rings closed but none separates alone (fertility is genus 4, every ring loops a handle); ring_02/ring_16 share 24 vertices and ring_04/ring_17 share 29 (near-duplicate rings), leaving 7 two-face sliver regions. Clicks via /input/click: click base -> region 0; Shift+click adds regions 2 and 7; B + clicks near ring_15 and ring_03 -> region 6; ring_09 + ring_03 -> region 5 (orange arm). Ctrl+S on the copy wrote select="between ring_09 ring_03" and the reload restored region 5. Screenshots: tmp/craw32_regions_fertility.png, tmp/craw32_click_shift_click.png, tmp/craw32_between_ring_15_ring_03.png, tmp/craw32_between_ring_09_ring_03.png. Not done: CRAW-24 is unimplemented, so DoD 4 holds only as "RingRegions is the shared computation"; a todo on CRAW-24 points at it.

2026-10-03 rework (R1-R5), uncommitted in worktree craw-32. One editing scene: RingScene (id ring-tool, window 'Mesh Edit') hosts EditTool implementations (new interface ixdar.scenes.ring.EditTool: toolName, activate, deactivate, perFrame, addControls, escape); tools = [RingTool, RingRegionTool]. Tab cycles the active tool and is the first control hint ('switch tool (now ...)'); the controls list is rebuilt on each switch, so only the active tool's keys and mouse bindings exist (ring: click/drag anchor/Del/Backspace/Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z/Ctrl+Y/Enter; regions: click, Shift+click, C clear); shared: Ctrl+S save rings, N ring numbers. Switching keeps the rings, an open draft and the region selection (kept as picked surface points). The R start/finish key is gone: the ring tool is simply the active tool at start, and Esc discards a draft or opens the menu. Regions are rebuilt from RingTool.liveRingMarks() whenever RingTool.ringRevision changes (any ring edit, delete, undo, save or graph reload). Ring numbers and lines are the ring tool's own MeshOverlayRuntime overlay in both tools (no second label code), so N and depth hiding are the same. Removed: RingRegionScene and its scene id ring-regions, the top-left text block (status goes to the log with [ring-regions] / [mesh-edit] prefixes), Ctrl+S select= saving, between mode (B key, RingRegions.between, the 'between' term, RingRegions.selectQuery, ringIndex). ring_regions node keeps region/point terms. Launch entry 'CRAW-32: ring regions on fertility' replaced by 'CRAW-32: ring and region tools on fertility (tmp copy)' (ring-tool on ../tmp/craw32_fertility_rings.dsl); the user's 'Ring Tool' entry unchanged. Verification on fertility (14 rings, tmp copy): region tool 11 regions from 14 closed rings; click on base -> region 0, Shift+click on arm -> adds region 5 (2 of 11); back to ring tool: plain shading, rings kept; drafted + confirmed a new leg ring, Tab -> 12 regions from 15 rings with the 2-region selection kept; Ctrl+S wrote only the ring to the tmp copy; fixture untouched. Screenshots: tmp/craw32_ringtool_numbers_view1.png, tmp/craw32_regions_view1.png, tmp/craw32_regions_view2.png (two orbits), tmp/craw32_region_click.png, tmp/craw32_region_shift_click.png, tmp/craw32_back_to_ringtool.png, tmp/craw32_ring_added.png, tmp/craw32_regions_after_ring_added.png, tmp/craw32_ringtool_numbers_hidden.png. mvn -q compile clean; mvn test 349 run, 0 failures (RingRegionsTest 4/4, between assertions replaced by point/region terms); ixd wt done passed.

Round 3 (items 7-9), 2026-10-03.
Item 7, rings through the model. Cause confirmed on fertility (13 spline rings, 896 segments): the old path (SurfaceFaceLocator.appendSegments, nearest face to each segment midpoint within 1e-4 of the bounding diagonal = 0.026) missed on 760 of 896 segments (85%), which got zero normals the line shader never drops. Per ring ring_05..ring_17: 73/98, 159/191, 75/94, 46/52, 46/49, 48/53, 55/63, 45/56, 32/33, 33/37, 65/79, 36/39, 47/52. The miss is because SurfaceSplineTracer emits the Euclidean cubic sampled at the geodesic's arc length, not the geodesic crossing: it sits off the surface by 0.33-0.65 on average and up to 3.1 (mean edge 2.2). That off-surface xyz also broke the depth tie (the shader follows the plane through the fragment's own position), so near-side spans dipped under the surface and far-side spans stuck out past silhouettes. Fix: SurfaceSpline keeps the trace's per-point pointVertexId / pointEdgeId / pointFraction and a surfacePolyline (vertex, or the exact geodesic crossing on the edge), set by SurfaceSpline.followPath; LineSet.pathStep builds each span's normals from the face(s) both points bound (two faces along an edge, as edge/vertexStep do); RingTool.splineLines draws rings and the draft/preview from them, graph edge-mask rings via LineSet.edge, and MeshOverlayRuntime.setLineGroups now takes that LineSet. After: 0 of 896 segments without a face normal and every endpoint on the surface (RingLineNormalsTest on fertility_rings.dsl). No depth bias; wireframe, embedded arcs, diagnostic lines and HalfEdgeMeshRuntime untouched (SurfaceFaceLocator still serves the diagnostic lines). SurfaceSpline.polyline (the saved/measured cubic) is unchanged.
Item 8: OrbitTool (scenes/ring/OrbitTool.java), a third EditTool that takes no clicks, drags or keys; the scene opens in it and Tab cycles orbit > ring tool > region select, named in the Tab hint.
Item 9: MeshNodeViewerScene.patchAndCollectionKeys (true by default) gates the K, P, Shift+P, D hints, their MeshViewerKeyGuy keys, the catalog log line and decomposePatches(); RingScene turns it off. The plain mesh-viewer still lists [ ] K Z P Shift+P D (tmp/craw32_meshviewer_controls.txt).

R9 / item 10 (camera not framed on open), 2026-10-03. Cause: MeshNodeViewerScene.initModel loads a -Dixdar.model choice through loadModelEntry, which wraps the load in ModelScene.preserveOrbit; that saved the absolute orbit distance before the load (initInput's CAMERA_DISTANCE_DEFAULT 3.5), frameMesh framed fertility at 268.5, and preserveOrbit then put 3.5 back. Logged on the CRAW-32 entry: frameMesh radius=107.4 dist=268.5 -> preserveOrbit restored dist=3.5. Same on mesh-viewer with -Dixdar.model (shared code, on master since loadModelEntry/requestedModel), and on every [ / ] or ml switch between models of different size (kept the previous model's distance). The -Dixdar.mesh.dsl path (user's Ring Tool entry, plain mesh viewer) never goes through preserveOrbit and was already framed at 268.5 headless; frameMesh's orbitMouse==null early return, uploadGraphOutput's frameCamera and the tools' activate() were ruled out by the log. Fix (ModelScene only): frameMesh records framedDistance and preserveOrbit keeps the zoom as a multiple of it, so an unzoomed view frames any model while a deliberate zoom and the orientation still survive a reload. Verified headless: Ring Tool and CRAW-32 entries open at target (23.93,-4.41,-0.20) dist 268.5 az 0.785 el 0.419, identical to mesh-viewer with either property; with a temp catalog (IXDAR_MODEL_DIR) ] / [ alternate torus_layout dist 3.375 (radius 1.35) and fertility dist 268.5, each framed. Screenshots tmp/craw32_r9_*.png (before_fix, open_*_entry, *_switch_next1..3/prev, meshviewer_*). mvn test 350 run, 0 failures; mvn -q compile clean; wt done passed.

Round 4 (items 11-12), 2026-10-03. Bindings in the editing scene (RingScene.setControls, listed first so a Ctrl hint wins over any plain one): ctrl+R ring tool, ctrl+T region select, esc orbit, ctrl+I menu (sceneModelMenu.toggle), the active tool's row marked '(active)'. RingScene.switchTool(EditTool) replaces Tab cycling; switching to the active tool is a no-op, so Esc in Orbit does nothing. Tab is unbound (in the scene it reaches nothing; with the terminal focused it is the terminal's own completion). EditTool.escape() is gone from the interface and the three tools; the ring tool's old Esc discard is now X (discard draft). ModelScene's 'escape: toggle the model scene menu' row is removed from the editing scene by RingScene (controls.removeIf), so no tool binds Esc or Ctrl+I. Hints shortened (region: 'select region', 'add / drop region', 'clear selection'; ring: 'remove anchor (or ring)', 'ring numbers'). Shared classes: OrbitCameraKeyGuy gets public boolean controlRResetsTarget = true (one field, one condition) because its keyCallback hard-bound Ctrl+R to the orbit-centre reset before scene keys; RingScene clears it, so the editing scene has no orbit-centre reset key (pan back with Shift+drag or frame). ui/State adds ringTool.activeTool (ACTIVE_TOOL constant). No change to ModelScene, MeshNodeViewerScene, MeshViewerKeyGuy, SceneModelMenu or MouseTrap.
Conflict audit: Ctrl+R was taken by OrbitCameraKeyGuy (fixed as above); KeyActions has no Ctrl+R/T/I (its Ctrl set is P,G,S,Q,F,C,V,A,E,N,B); MeshViewerKeyGuy handles only Z, [, ], P, K, D; Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Shift+Z/Ctrl+Y/Ctrl+S unchanged; no plain R, T or I hint in the scene. Plain R: KeyGuy.keyReleased fires KeyActions.Reset -> camera.reset() (suppressed while Ctrl is held; fires if Ctrl is released before R) and changes nothing on screen because OrbitMouseTrap owns the camera (screenshots identical, rmse 0). Plain T and I: not consumed. Terminal: scene hints fire even while the terminal is focused (OrbitCameraKeyGuy.keyCallback never checks IsTerminalFocused), so Ctrl+R/T/I and Esc switch tools / toggle the menu while typing; pre-existing for every hint (Enter, Backspace, N, C, Ctrl+S too), not fixed here. Automation /input/key delivers modifiers through the same keyCallback, so CTRL+R/CTRL+T/CTRL+I behave as typed.
Verification (launch entry on tmp/craw32_fertility_rings.dsl, fixture untouched, no Ctrl+S): opens in orbit; Tab in orbit and in ring tool: not consumed, tool unchanged; Esc in orbit: stays orbit; Ctrl+R/Ctrl+T from orbit, ring<->regions both ways, Esc from ring and from regions -> orbit (ui-state ringTool.activeTool each step); Ctrl+R with a panned target keeps the target; a draft (fingerprint 71d40e8eecbc7654) survives Ctrl+T then Ctrl+R and Esc then Ctrl+R, X discards it; Ctrl+I opens and closes the menu (sceneMenuVisible) from orbit, ring and regions.
